measures.title: Sonoma County Regional and Neighborhood Parks, Water, Wildfire Safety Sales Tax
measures.summary: Asks whether Sonoma County should continue its existing one-eighth-cent special sales tax countywide until ended by voters, providing about $15.5 million a year. Per County Counsel's impartial analysis, the money would fund regional and neighborhood parks and local city parks, including water quality, fire safety and accessibility projects under the measure's Expenditure Plan, with a special fund and annual independent audits.
measures.yesMeans: The County's one-eighth-cent parks sales tax is extended countywide until ended by voters.
measures.noMeans: The County may not extend this one-eighth-cent sales tax.

measures.title: City of Santa Rosa Community Safety/Financial Stability Measure
measures.summary: Asks whether Santa Rosa should replace its existing 0.50% sales tax (Measure Q, set to expire in 2031) with a 1% sales tax that continues until ended by voters, raising about $46 million a year. Per the City Attorney's impartial analysis, this would raise the total sales tax rate in Santa Rosa from 10.00% to 10.50%; it is a general tax the city may use for any lawful purpose, with priorities named for fire, 911 response, police, streets and homeless encampments, and annual audit reports.
measures.yesMeans: Santa Rosa's sales tax is reauthorized at 1% with no end date, replacing the current 0.50% Measure Q tax.
measures.noMeans: The current 0.50% Measure Q tax stays in place until it expires in 2031.
